title: SPIKE: Parse fillable fields from PDF
description:
Example code to grab all the form fields in a PDF and parse them into dicts:




 

```
import pdfplumber
from pdfplumber.utils.pdfinternals import resolve_and_decode

pdf = pdfplumber.open("/Users/ryanbagwell/Downloads/FY24-CSBG-Tribal-Annual-Report-Short-Form-Fillable-PDF-Tool_2.pdf")

fields = pdf.doc.catalog["AcroForm"].resolve().get("Fields")


def get_field_flags(flags: int | None):

positions= {
"read_only": 0,
"required": 1,
"no_export": 2,
"multiline": 13,
"password": 14,
"file_select": 15,
"multiselect": 22,
}

ifnotflags:
return \{k: Falsefork, _inpositions.items()}
 
bits=list((flags).to_bytes(32))

return \{k: bits[v] ==1fork, vinpositions.items()}


for field in fields:

data=field.resolve()

parsed= {
"type": resolve_and_decode(data.get("FT")),
"label": resolve_and_decode(data.get("TU") ordata.get("T")),
"name": resolve_and_decode(data.get("TM")),
"default_value": resolve_and_decode(data.get("DV")),
"choices": resolve_and_decode(data.get("Op")),
}

field_flags=resolve_and_decode(data.get("Ff"))

parsed.update(get_field_flags(resolve_and_decode(data.get("Ff"))))

print(parsed)

```

title: FIPS-199 Categorization
description:
It's the official categorization of your system's security impact level. You assess three dimensions:
||Dimension||Question||CSFEER Likely Rating||
|*Confidentiality*|What's the impact if data is disclosed to unauthorized people?|Moderate (PII of tribal recipients)|
|*Integrity*|What's the impact if data is modified or destroyed?|Moderate (reporting data accuracy matters)|
|*Availability*|What's the impact if the system goes down?|Low (not life-safety critical)|

Why it matters: The categorization determines which NIST 800-53 security controls you have to implement. A "Moderate" system has ~325 controls vs. ~125 for "Low" - significantly more documentation and security work.

This is typically one of the first ATO artifacts completed because everything else flows from it.

Confidentiality/Integrity/Availability impact levels assessed and justified; Overall system categorization documented (expected: Moderate); Categorization approved by ACF ISSO; Form submitted using NIST template

title: Fix Django deploy security warnings from manage.py check --deploy
description:
Running `manage.py check --deploy` identified 7 security warnings that should be addressed before production deployment:

1. **W004** - SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS not set (HTTP Strict Transport Security)
2. **W008** - SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT not set to True
3. **W009** - SECRET_KEY is insecure (django-insecure- prefix or too short)
4. **W012** - SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE not set to True
5. **W016** - CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE not set to True
6. **W018** - DEBUG is set to True in deployment
7. **W019** - X_FRAME_OPTIONS not set to DENY

Most of these should be configured via environment variables so local dev can keep DEBUG=True while production enforces secure settings.
